note: EGP/CEFR CV citations are from memory, not a live lookup. All 27 items per outcome (forms A, B, C) read.

egpPoints.point: Present simple affirmative, third person singular -s with common verbs
Present simple for habits/routines with frequency expressions (every day, at the weekend)
Wider range of verbs and contexts in present simple (spelling variants -es/-ies are orthographic, not a separate EGP point)

outcomes.itemsTest: A1 point. All forms test 3sg affirmative -s/-es/-ies in routine contexts (gap-fill, choice, error correction, free sentence, I->he/she transfer). Spelling variants (washes, cries, fixes, studies) add difficulty but no A2 grammar point; no negatives/questions with does, no contrast with other tenses.
outcomes.evidence: Form A items 1-3 drives/washes/cries; B fixes/flies; C brushes/studies; error items 'work->works', 'watchs->watches'; transfer 'I catch -> Omar catches'. Core form is EGP A1; A2 framing rests only on spelling load and full-sentence production.

egpPoints.point: Present continuous affirmative (am/is/are + -ing) for actions happening now
Present continuous with now/at the moment/Look!/Listen!
Present continuous contrasted with present simple; wider range of uses (e.g. temporary situations, 'working on' today)

outcomes.itemsTest: Mostly A1 point (affirmative, action now, auxiliary insertion). Item 4 in each form (knocks / is knocking, rings / is ringing, barks / is barking) and transfer C ('What are you working on today?') touch the A2 simple-vs-continuous contrast lightly.
outcomes.evidence: Gap-fills 'are playing/am cooking/is sleeping' (A), 'are painting/am waiting/is resting' (B), 'are climbing/am reading/is talking' (C); error items are auxiliary omission ('My sister talking', 'my father watch'). Only one choice item per form is contrastive. If contrast is the intended target, a split (A1 form / A2 contrast) would need more contrast items.

outcomes.currentLevel: A2 (reference: CEFR CV goods and services A1-A2; EGP can requests A1)

egpPoints.point: Can I ...? for requests/permission (Can I have ...?)
Would like / 'd like for wants and requests (I would like ...)
CEFR CV Transactions to obtain goods and services: A1 ask people for things and give people things; A2 ask for and provide everyday goods and services, order a meal

outcomes.itemsTest: A1 point. Items test fixed exponents Can I have ... please? and I would like ... please in simple shop/cafe settings; one-line hotel/pharmacy/bank transfer requests are near A2 transactional, but language remains formulaic A1.
outcomes.evidence: Gap-fills '___ I have' -> Can, 'I ___ like' -> would in all forms; choices between 'Give me'/'I want'/polite form; 'Make it polite: Give me the key -> Can I have the key, please?'; transfer 'I would like a new card, please.' Parent EN-L-A1-FN-polite-requests is itself A1; outcome is effectively A1 unless extended (Could I..., I'd like ... with follow-up exchange).
